handbookNote: Arkansas Real Estate Broker license exam. Part of the 2026-09-03 R26 population-tier broker buildout (population order: UT > NV > IA > AR > KS > MS > ID > NE > WV > HI > NH > MT > RI > DE > SD > ND > AK > VT > WY). Exam vendor: Pearson VUE, under contract with the Arkansas Real Estate Commission (AREC). Exam mechanics confirmed via Pearson VUE's own official Candidate Handbook (#090400, June 2026) and Content Outline (#090402, effective 12/1/2025). Broker candidates must hold an active salesperson/broker license for >=24 of the previous 48 months and complete 60 hours of education (45 hrs must be AREC's Broker Pre-License course) within 36 months preceding application. UNLIKE most other states' broker exams, Arkansas administers a single UNIFIED/comprehensive exam -- general/national and Arkansas-specific content are combined into one exam rather than separately-timed/scored national and state portions, and a failure requires retaking the entire exam (no partial retake of just one section). 120 scored items + 10 unscored pretest items (130 presented). Passing score: a proprietary SCALED score of 70 (explicitly not literal percent-correct or raw item count, per the handbook). Duration: handbook gives only a general 'two to four hours' range across all AR real estate exam types, no broker-specific minute figure published -- left unconfirmed rather than guessed; this site models it as 240 minutes (the top of that stated range) as a practice-session allowance. track_registry models this as exam_question_count=120, exam_duration_sec=14400, pass_percent=70, min_correct=84 (round(120*0.70)), consistent with this site's existing practice-approximation convention for scaled-score states (same as UT Broker). Real content outline (10 sections, % weight of the 120-item exam): Duties and Authority of the Real Estate Commission (4%, incl. the real Recovery Fund: $250,000 target balance, $25 fee cap, $25,000 per-violation/$75,000 per-licensee payout caps, actual-damages-only, A.C.A. 17-42-403 to 409), Arkansas Statutory Requirements Governing Licensure (10%), Other Arkansas Statutory Requirements (6%, incl. the real Arkansas Time-Share Act A.C.A. 18-14-101 et seq. and real Auctioneer's Licensing Board dual-jurisdiction rules), Federal Laws Governing Real Estate Activities (10%), Broker Operations and Responsibilities (18%, largest section -- supervision, trust accounts, recordkeeping, business organization, ethics, advertising, compensation), Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures (12%), Real Property Characteristics/Legal Descriptions/Condition/Inspection (10%), Property Valuation and the Appraisal Process (5%), Contracts/Financing/Settlement (15%, incl. Arkansas's real predominantly-non-judicial power-of-sale foreclosure process under the Arkansas Statutory Foreclosure Act A.C.A. 18-50-101), Property Management (10%, incl. Arkansas's real, distinctive status as the only state with no implied warranty of habitability and no repair-and-deduct remedy). Governing law: Arkansas Real Estate License Law, A.C.A. Title 17 Chapter 42, and AREC Commission Regulations. This bank was drafted across 10 parallel single-topic drafting passes (matching the real unified exam's own 10-section outline, since there is no separate national/state split to mirror). Answers were deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_broker_answers.js.
